title: Inequalities: what happens when the balance tips?
examples: Why does the inequality sign flip with a negative?

explain.say: In an equation the scale is level. But what if it tips? Look: x and 3 on the left, 7 on the right. The left side is heavier. So x plus 3 is greater than 7. Can you see which way it tips?

draw.text: Inequalities: what happens when the balance tips?

explain.say: Look at the 7 on the right. We write greater than with a sign like an open mouth, and the open side always faces the bigger amount. Like a hungry crocodile choosing the bigger meal!
Take 3 off both sides, just like an equation. The scale still tips the same way. Now x is greater than 4. Look at the x box. Is x just one number this time?
No! x can be many numbers. See the hops on the number line, starting after 4: 5, 6, 7, and on forever. Even 4.5 works. Is 4 itself allowed? No, because 4 is not greater than 4.

Super work! Now a wow. 2 is less than 5. But look: minus 5 is further left than minus 2, so minus 2 is greater than minus 5. When you multiply both sides by a negative, the sign flips! Challenge: solve x minus 2 is less than 6.

faq.a: It means greater than. The open side faces the bigger amount. So 8 is greater than 7 is written 8 > 7.
asks: What is the difference between > and <?

faq.a: It means x can be any number bigger than 4, like 4.5, 5 or 100. It is a whole range of answers, not one number.
No. For x greater than or equal to 4, written with a line under the sign, 4 is included. On a number line, an empty circle means not included and a filled circle means included.
asks: What is the difference between > and ≥?

faq.q: Why does the sign flip when multiplying by a negative?
faq.a: Multiplying by a negative mirrors numbers across zero. 2 is less than 5, but minus 2 is greater than minus 5, so the sign must turn around.
asks: Why do you reverse the inequality sign?

faq.q: How do you solve x minus 2 is less than 6?
faq.a: Add 2 to both sides, just like an equation. x is less than 8.

facts: The signs > and < were introduced by the English mathematician Thomas Harriot, in a book published in 1631.
Multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the sign.

quiz.say: Solve x plus 5 is greater than 9.
quiz.why: Take 5 from both sides and the sign stays the same: x is greater than 4.

wrong.1: 14 adds 5 instead of taking it away.
wrong.2: An inequality gives a range of answers, and 4 itself does not work.

quiz.say: Which number is in the answer to x is less than 3?
quiz.why: 2.5 is smaller than 3, so it fits.
